newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace takes Atlantic oil protest to court.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace takes Atlantic oil protest to court.

text.p: Greenpeace began a legal bid on Monday to halt oil exploration in the Atlantic, the environmental group said.
"We have lodged papers with the High Court seeking leave to present evidence against the government," said Greenpeace spokesperson Mirella Lindenfels.
Greenpeace wants the court to suspend exploration licenses granted to oil companies in the government's latest licensing round.
Greenpeace expects to hear from the court in the second week in July whether the case can proceed and its evidence against the government can be presented.

Lindenfels said the campaign group believed the government had failed to apply the European Habitats Directive when it awarded permits in the 17th offshore licensing round mainly in the Rockall Trough west of the Hebrides and north of the Shetland Islands earlier this year.

Today's legal challenge has its roots back in March when Greenpeace applied for all the oil licenses with the intention of turning the 22,000 square miles into a marine wildlife sanctuary. The bid was rejected by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the licenses were granted to 14 oil companies.
The DTI rejection of the Greenpeace license bid heralded the start of concerted campaigning via direct and legal action.
Last week Greenpeace activists sailed inflatable boats close to a Texaco oil exploration vessel in the north Atlantic in an attempt to stop seismic testing.
"It was partially successful in that Texaco agreed to stop testing while inflatables were in the area, but I understand testing resumed once the (inflatable) boats moved away," said Lindenfels.
Greenpeace declined to comment on the prospect of more direct action against other oil companies but further protests were not ruled out.
Greenpeace activitits earlier this month occupied the London office of U.S. oil company Conoco, another company awarded an Atlantic exploration license, for about four hours.
Two weeks ago Greenpeace campaigners seized the tiny, barren Atlantic Island of Rockall and rejecting British claims proclaimed a new state of Waveland.
